paras: The lynching at Marion, Louisiana, was the hanging of an unnamed Black man by a party of men pursuing a suspect in the killing of Luther Hayes, a white man, around October 29, 1888. The man was said to have been implicated in the killing in some way, while the accused shooter, Nathan Broadnax, remained at large. The only known report, carried by the Ouachita Telegraph of Monroe, also passed on expectations that more Black men near Marion would be killed.

According to the Farmerville Gazette, Hayes, about 35, was shot at Marion on a Saturday evening after demanding payment of a $10 debt from Broadnax, a Black man of about 20, and died about six hours later. The paper said Broadnax fired a shotgun loaded with squirrel shot into Hayes's side during the dispute.

Witnesses to the shooting chased Broadnax, but he escaped, and a posse continued the search. W. F. Millsaps, returning from Farmerville on Thursday, told the Telegraph that on Monday a party of men in pursuit had captured an unnamed Black man "implicated in the murder in some way," hanged him at an unstated place, and then riddled his body with bullets.

Millsaps described "considerable excitement in the parish" and said further trouble was expected. He reported that a colony of some 300 Black people lived near Marion and that the prevailing opinion held that several of their leaders would be killed before the excitement ended. Two deputies sent by Deputy Sheriff McGuire to aid the posse returned without finding it or the fugitive. No report of an inquest, arrests of the lynchers, or Broadnax's capture appears in the coverage.

The Ouachita Telegraph ran the Gazette's account on November 3 under the headline "ANOTHER HOMICIDE," a title that referred to Hayes's death rather than the hanging. The Gazette called the shooting a "deplorable affair" and hoped the posse would capture Broadnax, while the hanging appeared only in an appended paragraph, without comment, alongside the prediction of further killings. No other report of the hanging, in either the white or the Black press, appears in the coverage.

reader.title: Lynching at Marion, Louisiana (1888)
bases: A party of men pursuing the suspect in a killing captured another Black man said to be implicated, hanged him and shot his body (A1).

A 'party of men' with no stated lawful authority hanged a captured Black man accused of a part in a murder and riddled his body with bullets (A1); the size of the party is not given and the report is second-hand, from a traveler's account added to a reprinted Farmerville Gazette item (A1).
The hanging is known only from W. F. Millsaps's account appended to one Ouachita Telegraph article (A1); no other report was found.

accounts.label: Farmerville Gazette
accounts.gist: Broadnax, owing Hayes $10, quarreled with him, was disarmed of a plank, then shot Hayes with a shotgun and escaped; a posse pursued him.

accounts.label: W. F. Millsaps (to the Ouachita Telegraph)
accounts.gist: On Monday the pursuing party captured and hanged a Black man implicated in the murder and shot his body; Broadnax was still at large and more killings were expected.

framing.detail: Under 'ANOTHER HOMICIDE.' the paper treats Hayes's killing as the 'deplorable affair', wishes the posse success, and reports the hanging and expected killings of Black 'leaders' without condemnation.
